notable_absence.finding: This page has zero outgoing links and, more notably, no code on it overlaps in format with any of the codes 4_error.md (this batch) showed as worked examples when pointing readers here as 'the full list' - see cross_component_finding. Separately, several individual ICodes describe real constraints on concepts this batch has already minted (24007/24085: the Local link's name is system-reserved and cannot be operated on directly; 24144: primary indexes cannot be created on external collections; 24141/24127/24142: a scope or object cannot be dropped while still used by something else) that were not modeled as relations here, to keep this record proportional to a 240-row reference table rather than mining every row - recorded here in full so a reconciler mining this table further doesn't have to re-derive the observation that it's rich in this way.

cross_component_finding: 4_error.md (this batch) explicitly sends readers here with 'For a full list of error codes, see [Analytics Error Codes](error-codes.md)' after showing five worked syntax/identifier-resolution/type error examples, every one of which is reported with an ASX-prefixed internal code (ASX1001, ASX1077, ASX1074, ASX1073, ASX0002) wrapped in a generic 'Code: 1' envelope. Not one of those ASX codes, or anything resembling that prefix, appears anywhere in this page's ~240-row ICode table (which runs 20000-25000 and uses no letter prefix at all). The 'full list' promised on the referring page and the list actually delivered here are two different, non-overlapping numbering schemes for what is presumably the same underlying error surface (Couchbase Analytics is built on Apache AsterixDB, and ASX is a recognizable AsterixDB-internal code prefix) - a concrete, evidenced documentation inconsistency in the same shape as the eventing:lcb-key-eexists-error/lcb-key-enoent-error numeric-mismatch finding already on record, now found a second time in a completely different module. Recorded here as extraction-layer evidence only, per this round's extraction-only scope; not filed as a docs-issue.
cross_product_finding: Error 23003 ('Operation cannot be performed during rebalance') gives the SQL++ dialect warning's DDL family a topology-gating fact this batch's own 5_ddl.json record explicitly said it could not model: that page's notable_absence names the exact same restriction in prose ('No CREATE/DROP or CONNECT/DISCONNECT statement can be executed while the cluster topology changes') but declined to mint a relation for lack of a visible rebalance concept in the registry state it checked. server:rebalance turns out to already be promoted at the whole-registry level (not just this batch's extraction layer) - a case where checking a narrower registry view (this round's own digest excerpt) missed a term the full registry already had, the inverse of this round's usual fork-prevention concern about minting something that already exists under a different name.
